introduction: This spec gives the `speca` command its first writing form, the task form (`speca <spec> --task T --state S`), which moves one or more tasks of a spec package through afspec's task state machine all-or-nothing, writes through `Spec.Save`, and reports every change in the result envelope; it adds `--force`, `--dry-run`, claim suggestions in `next`, and the `envelope` types (`Change`, `CategoryLifecycle`, two warning codes) the form needs.

glossary.bypass: Setting a state with afspec's CompleteTaskStates (done) or ResetTaskStates (pending) instead of TransitionTask; reachable only through --force.
glossary.change entry: One element of the result's `changes`: {kind: "task", id, from, to, forced?} for a task whose state changed.
glossary.claim: A move of a task to in_progress. A claim of a task already in_progress is not a move, which makes the state machine the compare-and-set between agents.
glossary.legacy package: A package whose schema_version is neither 0 nor 2, by specr's rule.
glossary.move: A change of one task from its current state to the --state target; allowed exactly when afspec.ValidTaskTransition(current, target) is true (format v2 §8.3.1).
glossary.task form: The speca invocation `speca <spec> --task T --state S`, which changes task states; the first speca form that writes.
glossary.unknown key: A JSON key the v2 schema does not allow; LoadSpec drops it, ValidateSchema reports it as an unknown_field error, and a Save deletes it from disk.
glossary.writable package: A package Save would write: status draft, or status active without intent drift.

requirements.title: Task form flags and pre-load usage errors
requirements.rationale: A call that cannot hold must be refused before the package is touched, with the flag and values that fix it.

criteria.condition: speca is invoked with exactly one positional input, one or more --task flags and one --state flag whose values are valid
criteria.action: resolve the positional input as the report form resolves it, read each --task value as a comma-separated list of positive integer ids, `next` or `all`, and collapse duplicate ids into one

criteria.condition: --task is given without --state, or --state without --task
criteria.action: refuse the call and write nothing
criteria.contract: exit 2; error stage `usage`, category `usage`; no result

criteria.condition: the --state value is not one of pending, in_progress, done, dropped
criteria.action: refuse the call and write nothing
criteria.contract: exit 2; stage `usage`, category `usage`; fix_hint {flag: "--state", valid: ["pending","in_progress","done","dropped"]}

criteria.condition: a --task value is not a positive integer, `next` or `all` (including 0, a negative number and an empty item), or `next` or `all` appears together with any other --task value
criteria.action: refuse the call and write nothing
criteria.contract: exit 2; stage `usage`, category `usage`

criteria.condition: the task form is combined with --validate or --list
criteria.action: refuse the call as naming two operations and write nothing
criteria.contract: exit 2; stage `usage`, category `usage`

criteria.condition: the task form has no positional input, more than one, or a positional input that is `-`, a URL or spans more than one line
criteria.action: refuse the call and write nothing
criteria.contract: exit 2; stage `usage`, category `usage`

criteria.condition: --force or --dry-run is given without --task
criteria.action: refuse the call because the flag has no effect without a writing form
criteria.contract: exit 2; stage `usage`, category `usage`

criteria.condition: the resolved package fails to load
criteria.action: stop as the report form does
criteria.contract: exit 1; stage `load`, category `input`; no result

requirements.title: Post-load usage errors and expansion of next and all
requirements.rationale: Ids, `next` and `all` can only be checked against the loaded plan, and must resolve to the same tasks the report names.

criteria.condition: one or more named ids are not in the plan
criteria.action: refuse the call with a message naming the package and every unknown id; when the plan has no tasks the message says so
criteria.contract: exit 2; stage `usage`, category `usage`; fix_hint {flag: "--task", valid: [every task id]}, absent when the plan has no tasks; nothing written

criteria.condition: --task next is given and the plan has no next task
criteria.action: refuse the call with a message saying either that every task is done or dropped, or that no pending task has its dependencies done
criteria.contract: exit 2; stage `usage`, category `usage`; in the second case fix_hint {flag: "--task", valid: [the pending ids]}, otherwise none

criteria.condition: --task all is given on a plan with no tasks
criteria.action: refuse the call naming the package
criteria.contract: exit 2; stage `usage`, category `usage`

criteria.condition: the package's schema_version is neither 0 nor 2
criteria.action: refuse the call, with or without --force, with a message saying speca writes format version 2 only and a save would discard the v1 plan
criteria.contract: exit 2; stage `usage`, category `usage`; nothing written

criteria.condition: --task next is given and the plan has a next task
criteria.action: resolve `next` to the id that (*TasksV2Json).NextTask returns, the same task as the report's next_task

criteria.condition: --task all is given
criteria.action: resolve `all` to every task in plan order except tasks already in the target state and tasks in state dropped

criteria.condition: `all` resolves to no task
criteria.action: succeed without changing or writing anything
criteria.contract: exit 0; changes empty; summary `speca: <dir name> no task changed`; files and updated_at unchanged

criteria.action: move an explicitly named id as named even when the task is already in the target state, so that the state machine judges that move

requirements.title: All-or-nothing moves through the task state machine
requirements.rationale: A partial multi-task move leaves a plan no caller asked for, and the machine must be the only judge of a move.

criteria.condition: every named move passes ValidTaskTransition
criteria.action: check every named move before applying any, then apply them in plan order with TransitionTask, each on the copy the previous call returned

criteria.condition: any named move fails ValidTaskTransition and is not covered by --force
criteria.action: refuse the whole call without changing any task, with a message that names every refused task with its current state and the target, cites format v2 §8.3.1, and lists the states each refused task may move to
criteria.contract: exit 1; stage `task`, category `lifecycle`; tasks.json unchanged on disk

criteria.condition: a move is refused and the first refused task in plan order has at least one allowed target
criteria.action: carry that task's allowed targets, found by testing each of the four states with ValidTaskTransition, in fix_hint
criteria.contract: fix_hint {flag: "--state", valid: [states the first refused task may move to]}

criteria.condition: a move is refused and the first refused task in plan order is dropped
criteria.action: omit fix_hint and say in the message that --force with done or pending is the only way out
criteria.contract: exit 1; stage `task`, category `lifecycle`; no fix_hint

criteria.condition: a call names a task with target in_progress while that task is already in_progress
criteria.action: refuse the claim as a disallowed move, so a second agent learns the task is taken
criteria.contract: exit 1; stage `task`, category `lifecycle`; no task changes

criteria.action: for any plan, set of named ids and target state, either apply every named move or none of them, never a subset

requirements.title: Refusing writes the package status does not allow
requirements.rationale: A dry run must report the refusal the real call would hit, and Save would refuse these packages anyway.

criteria.condition: the package status is sealed, superseded or archived
criteria.action: refuse the call before any move is checked, with a message that its tasks can no longer change and a change is a new package that supersedes it
criteria.contract: exit 1; stage `status`, category `lifecycle`; no fix_hint; nothing written

criteria.condition: the package is active with intent drift, including a body without `## Intent` while intent_hash is set
criteria.action: refuse the call before any move is checked, with a message that the library refuses every write until the intent matches its hash again
criteria.contract: exit 1; stage `status`, category `lifecycle`; no fix_hint; nothing written

criteria.action: apply the status refusals of 11-REQ-4.1 and 11-REQ-4.2 identically with --dry-run and with --force

criteria.condition: Spec.Save returns a *LifecycleError or an *IntentError
criteria.action: report the failure at the status stage
criteria.contract: exit 1; stage `status`, category `lifecycle`

criteria.condition: the package is a draft, or active without intent drift
criteria.action: accept task changes

requirements.title: --force through the library's bypasses
requirements.rationale: Recovery from a wrong state must be possible without writing a state by hand.

criteria.condition: --force is given and the target is done or pending
criteria.action: make each named move the machine refuses with CompleteTaskStates (done) or ResetTaskStates (pending), and every allowed move with TransitionTask

criteria.condition: a task is set through a bypass
criteria.action: name the task with its from and to states in one high-severity task_state_forced warning at stage task, and mark its change entry forced
criteria.contract: warning {code: "task_state_forced", severity: "high", stage: "task"} per bypassed task; change entry carries `forced: true`

criteria.condition: --force is given and a named task is already in the target state
criteria.action: produce neither a change entry nor a warning for that task

criteria.condition: --force is given with target in_progress or dropped and a named move is refused by the machine
criteria.action: refuse the call as in 11-REQ-3.2, saying in the message that --force cannot set in_progress or dropped
criteria.contract: exit 1; stage `task`, category `lifecycle`; no task changes

criteria.action: let --force skip only the machine refusals of 11-REQ-5.1 and the unknown-key refusal of 11-REQ-6.3, never a usage error, the status refusal or the legacy-version refusal
criteria.contract: a usage error with --force still exits 2 at stage `usage`; a status or legacy-version refusal with --force exits as it does without --force

requirements.title: Readiness and validity warnings and the unknown-key guard
requirements.rationale: Recording work should not wait on a dangling id, but a save that silently deletes keys is data loss.

criteria.condition: a task is moved to in_progress while IsReady reports it not ready on the plan as it was before the call
criteria.action: go ahead with the move and raise a low-severity task_not_ready warning naming the task and the ids in its depends_on that are not done
criteria.contract: warning {code: "task_not_ready", severity: "low", stage: "task"}

criteria.condition: the package does not validate and validation reports no unknown_field error
criteria.action: go ahead with the task change and raise one low-severity spec_invalid warning naming the failing rules (distinct Check, else Category)
criteria.contract: warning {code: "spec_invalid", severity: "low", stage: "validate"}

criteria.condition: validation reports unknown_field errors and --force is not given
criteria.action: refuse the call before anything is written, with a message listing each artifact and key that the write would delete
criteria.contract: exit 1; stage `validate`, category `invalid_spec`; no fix_hint; files unchanged

criteria.condition: --force is given and validation reports unknown_field errors
criteria.action: go ahead with the write and raise one high-severity spec_invalid warning naming the keys the write removed
criteria.contract: warning {code: "spec_invalid", severity: "high", stage: "validate"}

criteria.action: raise at most one spec_invalid warning per call

requirements.title: Writing the change and reporting it
requirements.rationale: A caller must learn what the call did from the result alone, and an idempotent call must leave the files untouched.

criteria.condition: at least one task changes and --dry-run is not given
criteria.action: set updated_at to the current time in UTC formatted as RFC 3339, then write the package with Spec.Save(spec.Dir)
criteria.contract: tasks.json holds the new states; prd.md frontmatter holds the new updated_at

criteria.condition: Spec.Save returns a *SaveError
criteria.action: report a write failure with a message saying a failure while writing temporary files leaves the package unchanged, a failure during the final renames may leave some files updated, and the caller should run `speca <spec>` to see the state
criteria.contract: exit 1; stage `write`, category `disk`, retryable false

criteria.condition: no task changes
criteria.action: write nothing and leave updated_at unchanged
criteria.contract: exit 0 unless refused; package files byte-identical

criteria.condition: the call succeeds
criteria.action: return the report of the package computed on the state written, with every field the report form produces, plus `changes`: one entry per changed task in plan order
criteria.contract: exit 0; result.changes = [{kind: "task", id: N, from: S0, to: S1, forced?: true}]

criteria.action: write the summary as `speca: <dir name> task N <from> → <to>` for one change, `speca: <dir name> tasks N, M → <to>` for several, and `speca: <dir name> no task changed` for none, appending ` (dry run, nothing written)` under --dry-run
criteria.contract: envelope summary string

criteria.condition: the call is refused at stage status, task or validate, or fails at stage write
criteria.action: return the report of the package as it is on disk, without changes and without next
criteria.contract: exit 1; result present with current task states; `changes` and `next` absent

requirements.title: --dry-run
requirements.rationale: An agent must be able to see the exact effect of a call before making it.

criteria.condition: --dry-run is given with the task form
criteria.action: run every check, expansion, warning and refusal of the task form and skip the write
criteria.contract: package files byte-identical after the call

criteria.condition: --dry-run is given and the call would succeed
criteria.action: return the result the call would have produced, including the would-be updated_at and the changes it would have made, with dry_run set
criteria.contract: exit 0; result.dry_run = true; result.changes as the real call would report

criteria.condition: --dry-run is given and the real call would be refused
criteria.action: return the same refusal
criteria.contract: same exit code, stage, category and fix_hint as the call without --dry-run

criteria.condition: --dry-run is given and the call would change at least one task
criteria.action: set next to one entry: the same call without --dry-run, naming the resolved ids comma-joined instead of `next` or `all`, and keeping --force when it was given; with no changes next is empty
criteria.contract: next = [{tool: "speca", input: <spec_dir>, flags: ["--task", "N,M", "--state", S, ("--force")]}]

requirements.title: Claim suggestions in next
requirements.rationale: An agent should be led from the report to the claim and from each move to the call after it.

criteria.condition: the report form runs on a writable package
criteria.guard: no task is in_progress and next_task is a ready pending task
criteria.action: add to next the claim `speca <spec_dir> --task N --state in_progress` for next_task
criteria.contract: next contains {tool: "speca", input: <spec_dir>, flags: ["--task", "N", "--state", "in_progress"]}

criteria.condition: the list form runs
criteria.action: add to next the claim of the ready pending task of the first active package in number order that has no task in progress, has a ready pending task and has no intent drift

criteria.condition: a move succeeds without --dry-run
criteria.action: set next to the report's next computed on the package after the call, so a claim is followed by `specr <spec_dir> --task N` and a done by the next ready task's claim, or nothing when no task is left

criteria.condition: the task form fails or is refused
criteria.action: leave next absent from the envelope
criteria.contract: envelope next absent

requirements.title: Envelope additions and self-description
requirements.rationale: Programs consume the result through envelope and --schema, so the new fields must be typed and described.

criteria.action: define CategoryLifecycle = "lifecycle", for which RetryableFor returns false, without changing the meaning of any existing constant or type
criteria.contract: RetryableFor(CategoryLifecycle) == false

criteria.action: define WarnTaskNotReady = "task_not_ready" and WarnTaskStateForced = "task_state_forced" in envelope, with aliases in internal/cli and warnStages entries at stage task
criteria.contract: WarnStage of each code == "task"

criteria.action: define the Change type with kind, id, from, to and forced, where kind is an open string set and id, from, to and forced are omitempty, and add changes and dry_run, both omitempty, to AdminResult
criteria.contract: DecodeSpeca round-trips changes and dry_run; a result without them encodes neither key

criteria.condition: speca is invoked with -h or --help
criteria.action: describe the task form, --task, --state, --force and --dry-run in the help text

criteria.condition: speca is invoked with --schema
criteria.action: describe --task, --state as an enum of the four states, --force, --dry-run, the changes and dry_run result fields, and exit codes 1 and 2 covering refusals
criteria.contract: output equals the regenerated golden file cmd/speca/testdata/schema.golden.json

execution_paths.title: An agent claims the next ready task, then finishes it

steps.action: runs `speca <spec>` and reads the claim suggestion `speca <spec_dir> --task N --state in_progress` in next
loads the package, confirms it is writable, resolves next to NextTask's id and checks the move with ValidTaskTransition
TransitionTask returns the plan with task N in_progress
sets updated_at in UTC RFC 3339 and writes the package with Spec.Save
emits exit 0 with changes [{kind: task, id: N, from: pending, to: in_progress}] and next `specr <spec_dir> --task N`
runs `speca <spec> --task N --state done` and tasks.json on disk holds task N done

execution_paths.title: A second agent's claim of a taken task is refused

steps.action: runs `speca <spec> --task N --state in_progress` while task N is already in_progress
loads the package and finds in_progress → in_progress is not allowed by ValidTaskTransition
writes nothing and emits exit 1, stage task, category lifecycle, fix_hint {flag: --state, valid: [pending, done]}, and the on-disk report without changes or next

execution_paths.title: A dry run of a forced recovery, then the real call

steps.action: runs `speca <spec> --task 3 --state pending --force --dry-run` on a task that is dropped
plans the move through ResetTaskStates, raises a high task_state_forced warning, and skips the write
emits exit 0 with dry_run true, changes [{kind: task, id: 3, from: dropped, to: pending, forced: true}] and next `speca <spec_dir> --task 3 --state pending --force`
runs the suggested call, and speca writes the package with Spec.Save so tasks.json holds task 3 pending
